teacher_instructions: Play original Super Mario Bros. Move right toward the flag and avoid enemies and gaps. y increases downward; velocities are signed engine units. tiles are row-major 13x9, starting at y=32, columns from floor(player.x/16)-2. 0 means empty, positive bytes are terrain, -1 unknown. Grounded means player state 0. Simulation continues during request latency. Choose a controller action; do not invent a button. Jump must be released between jumps. This is an independent 60Hz recreation. Prediction velocities are pixels per frame. horizon_ms is the previous browser round trip (1000ms initially), not a guaranteed future delay. contact_ms uses current velocity, run_contact_ms assumes running at 2.6 px/frame. projected_gap is a constant-velocity estimate at reply arrival; negative means possible contact before the reply. Estimates ignore acceleration, terrain and enemy activation. Consider whether running would cause contact before the next answer; jump timing and releasing a held jump matter. null means unavailable, not safe. Experimental offline teacher: choose controls for the next 6 simulation frames (100 ms at 60 Hz), with no network delay. The objective is to progress right and survive; jump early enough to avoid enemies, holes and pipes. Release jump on landing before initiating the next jump.
teacher_context: fixed numeric synthetic checkpoint states, not live gameplay; 100ms intended action hold
